title: AI revenue is exploding. So is the compute bill

voiceover.text: At the end of twenty twenty-four, Open A.I. was earning over five times what Anthropic did.
Less than two years later, it's behind.
This is annualized revenue: the yearly pace each company is earning at. Anthropic went from one billion dollars, to seventy-one billion.
Open A.I. grew too, from five and a half billion to fifty. But the lines crossed in spring twenty twenty-six.
By October, Anthropic reached eighty-one billion.
But earning more isn't the same as making money.
In twenty twenty-five, Open A.I. brought in thirteen billion dollars. Its cloud compute bill? About sixteen billion.
Anthropic: four and a half billion in, nearly seven billion out on compute.
The gap is narrowing. But it's still a gap.
So who covers the difference? Investors.
In the first ten months of twenty twenty-six, these companies raised two hundred eighty billion dollars. More than double all earlier years combined.
So when the investor money slows down, who pays?
